storyboard.ears: Satellites caught the ocean quietly changing color, and scientists aren't sure what it means.
Twenty years of NASA satellite data show 56 percent of the ocean's surface now looks different.
storyboard.evidence: Nature / MIT (B.B. Cael et al.) | Share of ocean surface that changed color (2002-2022) | https://news.mit.edu/2023/study-oceans-color-changing-climate-change-0712 | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: A 2019 climate model predicted about half the ocean would shift color -- satellites found a bit more than that.
storyboard.evidence: Nature / MIT (B.B. Cael et al.); model by Stephanie Dutkiewicz (2019) | Predicted vs observed share of ocean that would change color | https://news.mit.edu/2023/study-oceans-color-changing-climate-change-0712 | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: The changed area covers roughly 203 million square kilometers, bigger than every continent on Earth combined.
storyboard.evidence: Nature / MIT (B.B. Cael et al.) | Area of ocean that changed color vs all land on Earth | https://news.mit.edu/2023/study-oceans-color-changing-climate-change-0712 | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: Nobody knows yet what it means for the sea life down there, or for us.
